title: Enterprise SDK priority gate and routing heuristics for multi-lang auth & streaming ergonomics
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We continue to see a rising volume of enterprise requests asking for combinations of: new language bindings (e.g., Kotlin, Go-native idioms), non-standard auth flows (mutual TLS, rotation-friendly short-lived tokens, client credential proxies), and streaming ergonomics (server-initiated reconnects, resumable streams, per-message metadata). Current intake is ad hoc: PM triages requests individually, and eng/design get surfaced late which increases discovery time and churn.

Goal: Define a repeatable priority gate and routing heuristics so we can classify incoming SDK/client library requests and take consistent, data-driven decisions about: 1) what we build in the short-term, 2) what we defer to partners or guides, and 3) what requires dedicated engineering scheduled into Dedicated/Private roadmaps.

Deliverables: 
- A 1-page priority gate rubric for SDK intake that balances customer impact, implementation cost, compatibility complexity, and security risk.
- A routing matrix that maps request characteristics to outcomes (e.g., quick docs + sample -> UX-only, design spike -> PM+Design, full engineering feature -> ENG roadmap ticket).
- Auth pattern decision catalog: patterns we support (Bearer token, rotating short-lived, mTLS, KMS-backed service accounts) and guidance on when to require security review.
- Streaming ergonomics guidance: recommended server and client behavior for reconnects, resume tokens, backpressure, and language-specific idioms to prefer.
- Template response emails and intake form fields for Sales/CS to collect required info.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Priority rubric reviewed and approved by Core PMs and two engineering leads.
- Routing matrix validated against 10 recent enterprise requests (samples in attachments) with proposed outcome for each.
- Auth catalog includes migration notes and required audit entries for Private deployments.
- Draft guidance merged into Confluence and linked from intake form; CS/Sales briefed.

Out of scope: building new language bindings or implementing long-term infrastructure changes — those will spawn separate ENG tickets after routing decision.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Being too permissive will increase maintenance burden; too strict will push customers away or cause shadow SDKs.
- For mTLS and HSM/KMS integrations we must factor in Dedicated/Private constraints (networking, key access).

Next steps:
1) Run a 1-hour intake workshop with Solutions Engineering and two customer reps (Mar 10-12).
2) Draft rubric and matrix (owner: PM) by Mar 13.
3) Engineering tech review and sign-off by Mar 18.
4) Publish guidance and update intake form by Apr 02.
